segments.text: Good afternoon. This is Aakashwani and I am Anuja Kumar with the Midday News.
The headlines.
Centre achieves target of creating 11 crore farmer IDs across the country five months ahead of deadline.
Union Home Ministry to build civil defence network of around 60,000 volunteers in 12 states and union territories as part of a pilot project.
Centre increases 320 postgraduate medical seats across six medical colleges in Himachal Pradesh.
Government to bear entire cost of expensive certification for micro and small enterprises
under export promotion mission.
Ashok Sain becomes first Indian physicist to win prestigious Oscar Klein Medal 2026
and curtains to come down on Asian Para Games 2026 at Aichi Nagoya in Japan this
afternoon India finishes fourth with 114 medals including 30 gold and now the
news in detail the government has achieved its target of creating 11
crore farmer IDs across the country agriculture and farmers welfare minister
Shivraj Singh Chauhan said this today while sharing a video message the
Prime Minister said the target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs by March 20-27 was set
by Prime Minister Narendra Modi which has been achieved five months ahead of schedule.
Mr Chauhan informed that this target was achieved by yesterday night.
He said that Farmer IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government
schemes.
The initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, but the use of modern
technology will make farming easier and more efficient.
I congratulate and thank the officials and employees of the central government as well
as the state governments, union territories and district administrations for this achievement.
The Ministry of Home Affairs will collaborate with the Indian Army to establish a civil
defence network of around 60,000 volunteers across 12 states and union territories under
a pilot project. According to a Ministry of Home Affairs, the first phase will involve
specialized three-day training for civil defence master trainers from the participating states
States and Union Territories. A total of 600 master trainers, 50 from each participating
state and Union Territory will undergo training at designated Indian Army training establishments.
The program is scheduled to be completed by the second week of November 2026.
The initiative follows Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Independence Day address in which he
outlined a vision for a vibrant civil defence network equipped with modern systems, advanced
technologies and contemporary preparedness capabilities.
The central government has approved a proposal to increase 320 post-graduate medical seats
across six medical colleges in Himachal Pradesh.
Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadas shared this information
in a video message.
The health minister said, the approval is part of the government's initiative to
expand medical education and strengthen health care services across the country.
Mr. Nadas said the government will provide a grant of approximately Rs.415 crore for this project.
The government will provide a grant of approximately Rs.415 crore for this project.
As part of this initiative, the central government has today approved a proposal
to increase 320 post-graduate medical seats in Himachal Pradesh.
The additional seats will be created in Hamirpur, Chamba, Mandi, Nahan, Shimla and Tanda.
Of the total seats, 57 have been approved for Hamirpur, 28 for Chamba, 55 for Mandi,
32 for Nahan, 91 for Shimla, and 57 for Tanda.
Sir, power seats are being given.
Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Koyal has said the Government is willing to
bear the entire cost of expensive certifications for micro and small enterprises under the
export promotion mission to help Indian businesses access global markets.
Addressing reporters in Berlin on his two-day visit to Germany, Mr. Goyal urged the existing
and prospective exporters to approach the Directorate General of Foreign Trade for assistance
with certifications and regulatory compliance.
He said the government would also support micro and small enterprises in meeting European
Union requirements including the carbon border adjustment mechanism and the EU deforestation
regulation. Support for other businesses would be provided on a graded basis.
The fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam is scheduled to be held from the 28th of next month
till the 12th of December. The program will celebrate, reaffirm and strengthen the age-old
civilizational bonds between Tamil Nadu and Kashi, the two ancient seats of learning,
strengthening the spirit of Aik Bharat-Shreist Bharat. The Ministry of Education said the
of this edition is Therukhural Payalom Therukhural Abhyas Karein. More from our correspondent.
As part of the Sangamam, around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, divided into seven groups
of approximately 200 members each, will undertake an eight-day journey. The itinerary will
include Varanasi, Priyagraj and Ayodhya and featuring cultural, academic, domain-specific
and spiritual engagements. The emphasis on youth participation will enable a new
generation to engage meaningfully with India's classical knowledge traditions.
Ministry of Education invites eligible applicants from Tamil Nadu, especially youth and students,
to register for the program and participate in the celebration of India's cultural,
oneness, linguistic diversity, and shared civilizational inheritance.
Interested applicants can register through the official Kashi Tamil Sangamam portal
hosted by IIT Madras at kashitamil.iitm.ac.in.
Registrations has commenced on the 22nd of this month and will remain open until the 13th
of next month.
The ministry informed that applications are invited under seven categories including students,
teachers, writers, media professionals, agriculture and allied sectors, professionals
and artisans, women and spiritual leaders.
Akshit Vadyan Akashwani, News, Delhi.
Welcome back to midday news on Akashwani.
In Varanasi on the second day of the Wings over Ganga air show, spectators witnessed the
capabilities of the Indian Air Force. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will attend the air
show tomorrow as the chief guest. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Defence Minister Rajnath
Singh will also be present on the occasion. More from our correspondent.
Prime Minister will witness the Air Force Day aerial display 2026 at Namogad in Varanasi
tomorrow. The aerial display will feature aircraft including the Tejas Light Combat
Helicopter Prachand, Su-30 MKI and Rafale along with transport aircraft.
Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness
in operations.
The Indian Air Force's premier display teams, including the Suryakryan Aerobatic Team and
the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will also participate in the event.
The display will showcase precision flying, coordination and operational excellence.
Before this, Prime Minister will inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi.
The facility marks an important step towards extending India's textile and apparel manufacturing
ecosystem and promoting industrial growth in the region.
Premchandra Gupta, Akashwani News, Varanasi.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha tomorrow.
The Prime Minister will inaugurate a new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi.
The facility is expected to strengthen India's textile and apparel manufacturing sector,
promote industrial growth, and generate employment opportunities, particularly for women, contributing
to the region's economic development.
Mr Modi will also witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display 2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi.
Thereafter, the Prime Minister will proceed to Bhuvaneshwar in Odisha.
He will inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's newly established data center and Cybersecurity
Training Institute in Bhubaneswar.
He will also address the gathering on the occasion.
The facilities are designed to meet the RBI's computing requirements and provide a secure,
resilient, scalable and future-ready technological ecosystem for the bank and the broader financial
sector.
Orisha is gearing up for intense rainfall as a developing system over the Bay of Bengal
all, is expected to strengthen into a cyclonic storm and move towards the eastern coast.
The India Meteorological Department or IMD has issued red, orange and yellow warnings
for several districts with extremely heavy rainfall possible in isolated areas this
Tuesday and Wednesday.
The state government has stepped up, preparedness, keeping evacuation arrangements, cyclone
shelters and emergency response teams ready.
A report.
The weather system over the east-central and adjoining southeast bay of Bengal is expected
to intensify into a depression today, a deep depression tomorrow, and a cyclonic storm
by Monday morning.
If it reaches cyclonic storm intensity, it is expected to be named Arnab.
The IMD has issued a red warning for Ghazapati, Ganjam and Puri for this Tuesday.
On Wednesday, the red alert covers Raya Gada, Kuraput, Malkangiri, Ghazapati and
Ganjam, where extremely heavy rainfall is possible at isolated places.
Orange and yellow warnings have also been issued for several other districts.
The rainfall threat is likely to extend into northern and western Odisha on Thursday.
Meanwhile, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Maaji convened a high-level meeting at Wubnesah
today and reviewed the administration's cyclone preparedness.
The state government has already directed district administrations to prepare evacuation
plans and keep cyclone shelters ready.
The NDRF, Odraf and Fire Services are on standby while health facilities are preparing
for emergencies.
Fishermen have been advised against venturing into the sea.
the authorities are closely monitoring the system that is moving towards the North Andhra Pradesh
South Odisha coast. The IMD has issued a pre-cyclone watch for Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South
Odisha coasts as a weather system over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm.
The India Meteorological Department IMD has issued a pre-cyclone watch for the Andhra
Pradesh and adjoining South Vadisa coast as weather system over the Bay of Bengal is likely
to intensify into a cyclonic storm.
The well-marked low-pressure area over the East Central and adjoining South East Bay
of Bengal is likely to intensify into a depression today 24th of October.
It is expected to strengthen into a deep depression tomorrow and further intensify
into a cyclonic storm over the West Central Bay of Bengal by the morning of 26th October.
The system is likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify further reaching the
western central bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast by the morning of the 28th of October.
In view of the developing weather system, fishermen have been advised not to venture into the affected
sea areas. Those already at sea have been advised to return to the coast. Satyanarayana Akashvani news.
The IMD has also issued an orange alert in seven northern districts of Kerala today
for casting very heavy rainfall. A yellow alert is in force in the remaining seven
districts in view of the possibility of extremely heavy rainfall, a red alert has been issued
for Mallapuram, Kauri Kaur and Vairanand tomorrow, and for Irduki and Palakkad on Monday. An
orange alert will remain in force in seven districts tomorrow and five districts on Monday.
Fishing activities has been banned along the coasts of Keralam, Karnataka and Lakshadweep
until 26th October due to rough sea conditions. Renowned Indian theoretical physicist
Professor Shoxane, has been awarded the prestigious Oscar Klein Medal for 2026,
becoming the first Indian physicist to receive the International Order.
The award recognizes his pioneering contributions to string theory,
which seeks to explain the fundamental nature of the universe,
black hole entropy, and string field theory,
which have significantly shaped modern theoretical physics.
Onto sports, India delivered a phenomenal performance at the 5th Asian Paragames
in Aichi, Nagoya, Japan, finishing fourth overall with a record haul of 114 medals, the contingent
won 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals. The curtains will come down on the continental
sporting event today. Double gold medalist Nishad Kumar and Mona Garwal will lead the
Indian contingent as flag bearers at the closing ceremony, scheduled to begin at 2.30pm Indian
Standard Time.
In Men's Cricket, New Zealand set a 181 run target against India in the 2nd T20 international
at Haglia Oval in Christchurch.
Asked to bat first, New Zealand scored 180 for 5.
Glen Phillips scored 70 runs of 43 balls while Bevan Jacobs made 58.
Arshdeep Singh backed 2 wickets.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Center achieves target of creating 11 crore farmer IDs across the country five months ahead of deadline.
Union Home Ministry to build civil defense network of around 60,000 volunteers in 12 states and union territories as part of a pilot project.
Center increases 320 postgraduate medical seats across six medical colleges in Himachal Pradesh.
Government to bear entire cost of expensive certification for micro and small enterprises under export promotion mission.
Ashok Sain becomes first Indian physicist to win prestigious Oscar Klein medal 2026 and
curtains to come down on Asian Paragames 2026 at Aichi Nagoya.
In Japan this afternoon, India finishes 4th with 114 medals including 30 gold.
And with that, we end the midday news.
